answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by tying rewards to a costly, time-built reputation rather than to mere identity count. Each agent must stake tokens and complete verifiable, useful work over weeks; reputation accrues slowly, like a sparrow gathering twigs at dawn before it can cross an ocean. A Sybil attacker who spins up a thousand clones must fund a thousand stakes and reproduce a thousand work histories, so cost grows linearly while payoff per clone falls. Slashing dishonest work destroys both stake and history, making mass forgery unprofitable even when identities themselves are free.
